_meta.purpose: Real Groq (qwen/qwen3.6-27b) token counts, captured once so future changes to the cross-provider comparison can be checked against real numbers without spending API calls again.
_meta.tier: free (no credit card) — 30 RPM / 1000 RPD for this model per console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits, checked before running
_meta.model_history_note: Originally planned second provider was Llama 4 Scout vision (preview) on Groq. Confirmed via Groq's own deprecation docs that this model was shut down 2026-07-17, before this project could use it. Switched to qwen/qwen3.6-27b, Groq's currently-offered vision model and its own recommended migration target.
_meta.headline_finding: Token cost is FLAT and INVARIANT to every pixel-space transform tested (downscale to 50% AND 10%, JPEG quality reduction, fixed-ratio crop) AND to the detail parameter (low/high/unset) - a second, independent provider showing the same qualitative pattern as Gemini 2.5 Flash. Unlike Gemini, Groq's detail parameter (the OpenAI-shaped equivalent of media_resolution) had ZERO effect, whereas Gemini's media_resolution did work (258->74 tokens). Groq's flat-cost behavior is therefore even more rigid than Gemini's.
_meta.verdict: The project's core technique (pixel-space region selection, adaptive budget allocation) has shown zero cost benefit on two independent real providers. Not proof of a universal law, but no longer explainable as a Gemini-specific quirk.

image_call.note: different order of magnitude from Gemini's flat 258 - itself informative

mechanism_check.note: unreduced vs uniform_downscale_50 on 4 real DocVQA samples - byte-identical on every sample

extreme_downscale_check.note: 10% scale (225x176, genuine thumbnail) on sample 49153.png - still flat

detail_parameter_check.note: sample 49153.png, unreduced image, varying only the detail parameter
detail_parameter_check.conclusion: No effect whatsoever - contrasts with Gemini's media_resolution, which DID change cost (258->74).

full_go_no_go_comparison.conclusion: Every pixel-space baseline (downscale, JPEG, crop, low-detail) is byte-identical to unreduced on every sample. Only ocr_everything/full_pipeline_hybrid differ, and they cost MORE (add OCR text on top of an already-fixed image cost).

fidelity_note.caveat: qwen/qwen3.6-27b is a reasoning model emitting a <think> block before its final answer. Initial run used max_tokens=300, entirely consumed by thinking on every sample - logged anls_score=0.0 for every row reflects TRUNCATED, not necessarily wrong, answers. Not a real fidelity comparison.
